title: How Dagobert launched a Twitter course to $30K in a month: landing page first, relationships, Black Friday
summary: Dagobert explains how he built and launched his Twitter course after growing his audience, covering validation via the landing page, a pre-built launch list, and a Black Friday retweet-for-discount mechanic. He also shares his view on pricing, perceived value, and preparing for platform risk.

principles.text: Write the landing page before building the product to test whether the promise is engaging and solves a big problem.
principles.quote: the first thing I did is I wrote the landing page

principles.text: Build a launch list during creation: offer to DM people you help when the product is out.
principles.quote: I would send them a reply saying hey you want me to send a DM when my course is out and so I had a list of 150 people like that

principles.text: Give generously for a long time; when you finally ask for launch support, people say yes.
principles.quote: I gave without thinking for so long that when I asked for once for some support they gave it and that was amazing

principles.text: Use a discount that requires a retweet so a link-bearing promo still gets reach and engagement.
principles.quote: I did basically 40 but if you retweet I give you 20 more so it's like 60 off if you retweet

principles.text: Perceived value tracks how close a product is to making the buyer money, which explains why courses outsell logos.
principles.quote: the closer you are to the money the higher the value

principles.text: Expect any platform or channel to end; keep savings, keep learning, and rely on portable skills like building an audience.
principles.quote: everything will end eventually so just prepare by having savings preparing that and always doing new stuff
